summary:
The bill, titled the "Halting the Epidemic of Addiction and Loss Act of 2025" (S. 2336, 119th Congress), directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to ensure that references to opioid overdose reversal agents in specified HHS grant programs are not limited to naloxone. The bill's operative mechanism is a mandate to construe or update regulatory and guidance references to encompass all FDA-approved opioid overdose reversal drugs.

Section 2(a) imposes a prospective, ongoing obligation: whenever the Department issues a regulation or guidance for any grant program addressing opioid misuse and use disorders, the Secretary shall ensure, "as appropriate," that any reference to an opioid overdose reversal drug (such as naloxone) is inclusive of any opioid overdose reversal drug approved under section 505 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 355) for emergency treatment of a known or suspected opioid overdose. The "as appropriate" qualifier and the FDCA section 505 approval standard condition the scope of this general rule.

Section 2(b) addresses existing references retrospectively. Under paragraph (1), not later than one year after the date of enactment, the Secretary shall update all covered references to be inclusive of any opioid overdose reversal drug "approved or otherwise authorized for use" by the FDA. Notably, this update provision employs a broader authorization standard ("approved or otherwise authorized") than the section 505 approval standard used in subsection (a).

Paragraph (2) delimits the covered references to those appearing in any HHS regulation or guidance that (A) was issued before the date of enactment and (B) is included in one of two specified grant programs: (i) the State and Tribal response to opioid use disorders grant program under section 1003 of the 21st Century Cures Act (42 U.S.C. 290ee-3a) (the State Opioid Response Grants and Tribal Opioid Response Grants); or (ii) the grant program for priority substance use disorder prevention needs of regional and national significance under section 516 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 290bb-22).

The bill amends no existing statutory text directly, contains no repeals or sunset provisions, and includes no authorization or appropriation of funds. Its sole enforceable deadline is the one-year update requirement in subsection (b)(1); the subsection (a) obligation applies on an ongoing basis upon enactment. The bill has been read twice and referred to the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
